blocks.content: Introduction to Power generation and regulation
Describe alternator/generator basics and voltage regulator function.

items.definition: Alternators are preferred in modern aircraft because: (1) they produce usable charging voltage at low RPM (including idle), and (2) they are lighter than generators of equivalent output. Generators require higher RPM to produce the same output and are heavier.
items.analogy: Like a newer, more efficient engine that makes full power from idle rather than needing high RPM to get going.

items.definition: The voltage regulator controls alternator or generator field current to maintain a consistent output voltage (typically 28V ±0.5V in aircraft). Without it, alternator output would vary with RPM and load, potentially overcharging the battery or under-powering avionics.
items.analogy: Like a thermostat for electrical voltage — it constantly adjusts to keep output steady regardless of engine speed or load.

items.definition: Capacitors and inductors (chokes) are used to filter alternator-generated electrical noise from the DC bus. Capacitors shunt high-frequency noise to ground; inductors block high-frequency noise from passing through. Together they form a low-pass filter keeping the bus clean for sensitive avionics.
items.analogy: Like a water filter — lets clean water (clean DC) through while trapping particles (electrical noise).

blocks.question: Why are alternators preferred over generators in modern aircraft DC electrical systems?
choices: They produce AC power directly usable by avionics
They produce usable output at lower RPM and are lighter weight
They require no voltage regulator for output control
They have higher internal resistance which protects against surges
blocks.feedback: The two key advantages: (1) alternators charge at low RPM — including idle — whereas generators need higher RPM to produce charging voltage; (2) alternators are lighter for equivalent output. Both matter greatly in aviation.

blocks.question: Which component is responsible for maintaining consistent alternator output voltage in an aircraft DC electrical system?
blocks.feedback: The voltage regulator monitors alternator output and adjusts field excitation to maintain the setpoint voltage. It compensates for changes in engine speed and electrical load to keep bus voltage stable.

blocks.question: Which components are used to filter and suppress alternator noise in an aircraft DC electrical system?
blocks.feedback: Capacitors and inductors form a filter network on the alternator output. Capacitors shunt high-frequency noise to ground; inductors block noise from reaching the bus. This protects avionics from electrical interference generated by the alternator.
